before.title: Headless loop guards: stop endless loops and searches
before.detail: Guards on every headless session the orchestrator launches (claude-headless.sh + agent-slots + the running-builds watchdog's afterTick hook in pipeline.mjs): 1) Hard caps per session: --max-turns, wall time and cost cap derived from the step estimates (e.g. 2x estimate), settings with defaults. 2) Step progress timer: no step tick within 1.5x the step's estimate -> warn note, at 2x -> stop the session, build back to pending with the reason. 3) Loop detector reading the live log: the same command/tool call (or near-identical grep/find/sed) repeated N times, or M searches in a row with no edit/commit -> stop and note. 4) Search budget per step (e.g. 15 greps/finds) written into the brief and enforced by the detector. 5) Every stop: build note with the reason and last log lines, AmberX notification (normal notification, not an alarm), slot released, no auto-relaunch of a looped step until Brett says. 6) Brief line: 'If you can't find something in 3 searches, stop and leave a note.' Settings in orchestrator settings (categorized sections), full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests with fake logs: repeated command, search spree, no tick, cost cap.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: "I need a way to manage the safeguards." Add a Safeguards panel (orchestrator settings, its own section, also reachable from the build's row): turn each guard on/off; edit turns cap, time cap (x estimate), cost cap, no-tick warn/stop multipliers, repeat-command count, search budget; per-build and per-queue overrides; a live view of each running session against its limits (turns, time, cost, searches used); a log of every guard stop with the reason, last log lines and buttons: Relaunch, Raise limit and relaunch, Send back to pending. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and a deep link. Stock controls, 3 layout options to UI Review.

Brett on managing the safeguards: "I don't want the file itself to be editable. I want it to be view. You can view the file with steps. Make it an MD file with bullet points for the rules. And create a sortable, collapsible tree with a whole shitload of different rules, of snippets. When you click it, it will pop a dialogue to let you add the custom fields that it requires for the snippet and it will insert it." Build: 1) The safeguards live as a Markdown rules file (one bullet per rule, grouped by heading), shown READ-ONLY in the panel (rendered view with the steps it applies to); no free-text editing. 2) A snippet library: a sortable, searchable, collapsible tree (category > sub-category > snippet) with a large set of ready rule snippets (turn caps, time/cost caps, no-tick timeouts, repeat-command and search-spree limits, file/folder fences, no sub-agents, model limits, test-before-commit, stop-and-note rules, etc.). 3) Clicking a snippet opens a dialog with the fields it needs (number, duration, $, path, model, scope: global/queue/build/step) with validation and a preview line; Insert adds the bullet to the rules file. 4) Each inserted rule can be toggled, moved, or removed from the panel (structured actions, still no raw edit); every change is versioned with history and undo. 5) The orchestrator and the loop detector read their limits from this file; the brief gets the bullets that apply to the step. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control; stock controls; 3 layout options to UI Review.

Brett: "the dialogue that needs custom parameters for the rules, any that are like file names or specific things already have a list to choose from for the custom parameters." In the snippet fields dialog, every field whose values already exist is a pick list (searchable dropdown or tree picker), not free text: file and folder paths (from the repo tree / plugin registry), plugins, apps, builds, queues, steps, Claude accounts, API accounts, models, agents/crew, tools, commands, settings keys. Multi-select where a rule takes several. Free text only for true free values (numbers, durations, $ amounts) and those get validated inputs with units.

Brett: "There has to be filters too, where you put in for the list of certain types of parameters. There's got to be filters." Every pick list in the snippet dialog has filters fitting its type, plus search: files/folders by app, plugin, folder, file type/extension, changed recently, owned by a build; plugins by app, category, enabled; builds by status, queue, model, category, date; queues by account type; steps by build and state; accounts by role, model available, health; models by tier; agents by role/skill; tools by service; settings keys by plugin/section. Filters combine, show counts, can be cleared, and remember the last used per field.

Brett: "list of features. Stack. And the list of predefined search terms based on what the rule is." 1) Filters stack (combine) and include a 'feature' filter: pick from the Shipped features list / plugin feature catalog to narrow files, builds and steps to one feature. 2) Each snippet carries predefined search terms and preset filter stacks that fit that rule (e.g. a file-fence rule offers 'server routes', 'web views', 'plugin.json', 'tests', 'schemas'; a model rule offers 'Fable-only steps', 'UI steps'), shown as quick chips in the pick list; tap one to apply. Brett can save his own presets per snippet.

origin.said: We need some safeguards in there to, to make sure their fucking headless sessions don't get stuck in endless loops and searches.

We need some safeguards in there to, to make sure their fucking headless sessions don't get stuck in endless loops and searches.
Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/headless-loop-guards-stop-endless-loops-and-sear.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: Headless loop guards: stop endless loops and searches
before.detail: Guards on every headless session the orchestrator launches (claude-headless.sh + agent-slots + the running-builds watchdog's afterTick hook in pipeline.mjs): 1) Hard caps per session: --max-turns, wall time and cost cap derived from the step estimates (e.g. 2x estimate), settings with defaults. 2) Step progress timer: no step tick within 1.5x the step's estimate -> warn note, at 2x -> stop the session, build back to pending with the reason. 3) Loop detector reading the live log: the same command/tool call (or near-identical grep/find/sed) repeated N times, or M searches in a row with no edit/commit -> stop and note. 4) Search budget per step (e.g. 15 greps/finds) written into the brief and enforced by the detector. 5) Every stop: build note with the reason and last log lines, AmberX notification (normal notification, not an alarm), slot released, no auto-relaunch of a looped step until Brett says. 6) Brief line: 'If you can't find something in 3 searches, stop and leave a note.' Settings in orchestrator settings (categorized sections), full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests with fake logs: repeated command, search spree, no tick, cost cap.

Brett: "as you type in the field, it automatically drops down the list of all the ones that match. Whatever you type. In real time. Letter per letter." # Build: one-builds-page-pending-queued-built-tabs-remove

## Brett said (verbatim)
> There's too many tables that show information about builds. Get rid of all of them. All we want is pending queued and built. All on one page in different tabs.

## What to build
Continue build "One builds page: Pending, Queued, Built tabs; remove every other builds table" (one-builds-page-pending-queued-built-tabs-remove) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"There's too many tables that show information about builds. Get rid of all of them. All we want is pending queued and built. All on one page in different tabs."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Brett: too many tables show build info. Remove all of them (Build Manager tables, orchestrator tables, tracker, steps, plan/queue views, duplicates in other plugins; keep code for harvesting). Replace with ONE page with three tabs: Pending, Queued, Built. All read the one builds store. Plan Studio stays for plans. Full API + voice + MCP/CLI control. 3 UI options to UI Review; shots; tests; report. Must create its Plan Studio plan.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

after.title: Shipped Features: live manifests from dispatch to done, badges + progress meter
after.detail: Builds on shipped-manifest-api (landed 79ed472c0f1f, shipped-manifest@1). Today the manifest is sent only when a build lands. Change: the orchestrator sends a manifest to Shipped Features (and Plan Studio, per the queued Plan Studio manifest build) at every event: when it dispatches the job, on every build update (model/account change, note, hold, guard stop), on every step completed, and on completion/land. Each manifest is versioned (sequence number, previous version kept as history) and validated. The Shipped Features entry exists from dispatch, not only after landing, and shows a live status badge (dispatched, building, step x/y, waiting on UI Review, held, stopped by guard, failed, landed, shipped) plus a progress meter (steps done / total, time and cost used vs estimate), updated in real time (live push, no refresh). History view per entry shows every manifest. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep link. Tests: dispatch creates the entry, each step tick bumps the version and meter, land sets shipped; invalid manifest is refused with the reason.

origin.said: Ship dock features gets manifest as soon as orchestrator sends out the job. then its status is it, it sends a manifest every time it's updated to every time it's a step completed it sends a manifest every time it's completed it sends a manifest and its status in ship features is updated constantly with different badges and a progress meter.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

steps.text: Switching the active account actually signs the VPS Claude login in to it (live login matches active), banner clock badge goes live
Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

New files are not listed. Keep the list short (the files that matter, not whole folders). Also trim the brief: Brett's words once (not twice), steps, files, how to tick steps; drop boilerplate that doesn't apply to the step (look/token rules only for UI steps). Tests: brief template lists files per step; a UI step gets the look rules, a non-UI step doesn't; Brett's words appear once.

before.title: Shipped Features: live manifests from dispatch to done, badges + progress meter
before.detail: Builds on shipped-manifest-api (landed 79ed472c0f1f, shipped-manifest@1). Today the manifest is sent only when a build lands. Change: the orchestrator sends a manifest to Shipped Features (and Plan Studio, per the queued Plan Studio manifest build) at every event: when it dispatches the job, on every build update (model/account change, note, hold, guard stop), on every step completed, and on completion/land. Each manifest is versioned (sequence number, previous version kept as history) and validated. The Shipped Features entry exists from dispatch, not only after landing, and shows a live status badge (dispatched, building, step x/y, waiting on UI Review, held, stopped by guard, failed, landed, shipped) plus a progress meter (steps done / total, time and cost used vs estimate), updated in real time (live push, no refresh). History view per entry shows every manifest. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep link. Tests: dispatch creates the entry, each step tick bumps the version and meter, land sets shipped; invalid manifest is refused with the reason.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

steps.text: Switching the active account actually signs the VPS Claude login in to it (live login matches active), banner clock badge goes live
Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: Shipped Features: live manifests from dispatch to done, badges + progress meter
before.detail: Builds on shipped-manifest-api (landed 79ed472c0f1f, shipped-manifest@1). Today the manifest is sent only when a build lands. Change: the orchestrator sends a manifest to Shipped Features (and Plan Studio, per the queued Plan Studio manifest build) at every event: when it dispatches the job, on every build update (model/account change, note, hold, guard stop), on every step completed, and on completion/land. Each manifest is versioned (sequence number, previous version kept as history) and validated. The Shipped Features entry exists from dispatch, not only after landing, and shows a live status badge (dispatched, building, step x/y, waiting on UI Review, held, stopped by guard, failed, landed, shipped) plus a progress meter (steps done / total, time and cost used vs estimate), updated in real time (live push, no refresh). History view per entry shows every manifest. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep link. Tests: dispatch creates the entry, each step tick bumps the version and meter, land sets shipped; invalid manifest is refused with the reason.

notes.text: Brett: "it lists what files were touched too, but they're hidden... in a collapsible, in an expanded row... you gotta expand a few things to get to them. They'll open in a dialog, which also you can click the files and open in a read-only editor. Checkbox to make it editable." Each manifest lists the files touched (added/changed/deleted, per step). In Shipped Features they sit tucked away: entry row > expand > Details > collapsed 'Files touched' section (grouped by step and folder, counts). Clicking it opens a dialog with the file list; clicking a file opens it in a read-only code editor (syntax highlight, diff vs before toggle). A 'Make editable' checkbox in the editor switches it to edit mode; saving goes through a normal commit with Brett's name and a change entry, never silent. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

steps.text: Switching the active account actually signs the VPS Claude login in to it (live login matches active), banner clock badge goes live
Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

origin.said: "The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs." Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."
origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

Also trim the brief: Brett's words once (not twice), steps, files, how to tick steps; drop boilerplate that doesn't apply to the step (look/token rules only for UI steps). Tests: brief template lists files per step; a UI step gets the look rules, a non-UI step doesn't; Brett's words appear once.

before.title: Shipped Features: live manifests from dispatch to done, badges + progress meter
before.detail: Builds on shipped-manifest-api (landed 79ed472c0f1f, shipped-manifest@1). Today the manifest is sent only when a build lands. Change: the orchestrator sends a manifest to Shipped Features (and Plan Studio, per the queued Plan Studio manifest build) at every event: when it dispatches the job, on every build update (model/account change, note, hold, guard stop), on every step completed, and on completion/land. Each manifest is versioned (sequence number, previous version kept as history) and validated. The Shipped Features entry exists from dispatch, not only after landing, and shows a live status badge (dispatched, building, step x/y, waiting on UI Review, held, stopped by guard, failed, landed, shipped) plus a progress meter (steps done / total, time and cost used vs estimate), updated in real time (live push, no refresh). History view per entry shows every manifest. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep link. Tests: dispatch creates the entry, each step tick bumps the version and meter, land sets shipped; invalid manifest is refused with the reason.

notes.text: Brett: "it lists what files were touched too, but they're hidden... in a collapsible, in an expanded row... you gotta expand a few things to get to them. They'll open in a dialog, which also you can click the files and open in a read-only editor. Checkbox to make it editable." Each manifest lists the files touched (added/changed/deleted, per step). In Shipped Features they sit tucked away: entry row > expand > Details > collapsed 'Files touched' section (grouped by step and folder, counts). Clicking it opens a dialog with the file list; clicking a file opens it in a read-only code editor (syntax highlight, diff vs before toggle). A 'Make editable' checkbox in the editor switches it to edit mode; saving goes through a normal commit with Brett's name and a change entry, never silent. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: "when you open the file, it will jump to the feature that you found it through and highlight it. In focus, centered in screen." The manifest records, per touched file, the line ranges each step/feature changed. Opening a file from a Shipped Features entry scrolls the editor to that feature's code, centers it on screen, and highlights the changed lines (theme highlight colour); if a feature touched several spots, next/previous buttons jump between them. Same when opened via API/deep link (file + feature + range).

origin.said: Ship dock features gets manifest as soon as orchestrator sends out the job. then its status is it, it sends a manifest every time it's updated to every time it's a step completed it sends a manifest every time it's completed it sends a manifest and its status in ship features is updated constantly with different badges and a progress meter.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).

before.title: Shipped Features: live manifests from dispatch to done, badges + progress meter
before.detail: Builds on shipped-manifest-api (landed 79ed472c0f1f, shipped-manifest@1). Today the manifest is sent only when a build lands. Change: the orchestrator sends a manifest to Shipped Features (and Plan Studio, per the queued Plan Studio manifest build) at every event: when it dispatches the job, on every build update (model/account change, note, hold, guard stop), on every step completed, and on completion/land. Each manifest is versioned (sequence number, previous version kept as history) and validated. The Shipped Features entry exists from dispatch, not only after landing, and shows a live status badge (dispatched, building, step x/y, waiting on UI Review, held, stopped by guard, failed, landed, shipped) plus a progress meter (steps done / total, time and cost used vs estimate), updated in real time (live push, no refresh). History view per entry shows every manifest. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep link. Tests: dispatch creates the entry, each step tick bumps the version and meter, land sets shipped; invalid manifest is refused with the reason.

notes.text: Brett: "it lists what files were touched too, but they're hidden... in a collapsible, in an expanded row... you gotta expand a few things to get to them. They'll open in a dialog, which also you can click the files and open in a read-only editor. Checkbox to make it editable." Each manifest lists the files touched (added/changed/deleted, per step). In Shipped Features they sit tucked away: entry row > expand > Details > collapsed 'Files touched' section (grouped by step and folder, counts). Clicking it opens a dialog with the file list; clicking a file opens it in a read-only code editor (syntax highlight, diff vs before toggle). A 'Make editable' checkbox in the editor switches it to edit mode; saving goes through a normal commit with Brett's name and a change entry, never silent. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: "when you open the file, it will jump to the feature that you found it through and highlight it. In focus, centered in screen." The manifest records, per touched file, the line ranges each step/feature changed. Opening a file from a Shipped Features entry scrolls the editor to that feature's code, centers it on screen, and highlights the changed lines (theme highlight colour); if a feature touched several spots, next/previous buttons jump between them. Same when opened via API/deep link (file + feature + range).

Brett: "Any failed, any errors that are file related get sent to the log with links to the file with the bad code there, the conflicted code, and highlighted and in focus." Every file-related failure (test/typecheck/lint/CI errors, merge conflicts, guard stops, parse errors in JSON) is written to the terminal log and the Shipped Features entry's manifest with file path + line range + message. Each log line carries a link; clicking it opens the file in the read-only editor scrolled to the bad or conflicted code, centered and highlighted (conflicts show both sides). Same via API/deep link.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Orchestrator view: all-profiles projection + filter + Profile column; bulk actions on visible builds
Pending, Queue and Plan tables: filter, Profile column, Filtered note
Tracker, Git status board, Crew: filter adoption
Bulk CLI/MCP (land-all, merge batch): resolveFilter + profiles argument; tests, shots, PR

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

before.title: Shipped Features: live manifests from dispatch to done, badges + progress meter
before.detail: Builds on shipped-manifest-api (landed 79ed472c0f1f, shipped-manifest@1). Today the manifest is sent only when a build lands. Change: the orchestrator sends a manifest to Shipped Features (and Plan Studio, per the queued Plan Studio manifest build) at every event: when it dispatches the job, on every build update (model/account change, note, hold, guard stop), on every step completed, and on completion/land. Each manifest is versioned (sequence number, previous version kept as history) and validated. The Shipped Features entry exists from dispatch, not only after landing, and shows a live status badge (dispatched, building, step x/y, waiting on UI Review, held, stopped by guard, failed, landed, shipped) plus a progress meter (steps done / total, time and cost used vs estimate), updated in real time (live push, no refresh). History view per entry shows every manifest. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep link. Tests: dispatch creates the entry, each step tick bumps the version and meter, land sets shipped; invalid manifest is refused with the reason.

notes.text: Brett: "it lists what files were touched too, but they're hidden... in a collapsible, in an expanded row... you gotta expand a few things to get to them. They'll open in a dialog, which also you can click the files and open in a read-only editor. Checkbox to make it editable." Each manifest lists the files touched (added/changed/deleted, per step). In Shipped Features they sit tucked away: entry row > expand > Details > collapsed 'Files touched' section (grouped by step and folder, counts). Clicking it opens a dialog with the file list; clicking a file opens it in a read-only code editor (syntax highlight, diff vs before toggle). A 'Make editable' checkbox in the editor switches it to edit mode; saving goes through a normal commit with Brett's name and a change entry, never silent. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: "when you open the file, it will jump to the feature that you found it through and highlight it. In focus, centered in screen." The manifest records, per touched file, the line ranges each step/feature changed. Opening a file from a Shipped Features entry scrolls the editor to that feature's code, centers it on screen, and highlights the changed lines (theme highlight colour); if a feature touched several spots, next/previous buttons jump between them. Same when opened via API/deep link (file + feature + range).

Brett: "Any failed, any errors that are file related get sent to the log with links to the file with the bad code there, the conflicted code, and highlighted and in focus." Every file-related failure (test/typecheck/lint/CI errors, merge conflicts, guard stops, parse errors in JSON) is written to the terminal log and the Shipped Features entry's manifest with file path + line range + message. Each log line carries a link; clicking it opens the file in the read-only editor scrolled to the bad or conflicted code, centered and highlighted (conflicts show both sides). Same via API/deep link.

Brett: "also make an errors column that's hideable. With a collapse button." In the Terminal plugin (console-terminal), add an Errors column: a side column next to the output showing only the file-related errors (file, line, message, build, time; click opens the file at the bad code, centered and highlighted). It has a collapse button (collapses to a thin strip with an error count badge) and can be hidden entirely from the Terminal toolbar/settings; state remembered. Filters by build, severity, plugin. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.
